title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate‑Verify‑Repair for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents; 400 paired episodes) to evaluate whether a deterministic verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM produces device configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by both baseline and guarded). Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.02; preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (primary confirmatory test). An exploratory paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04]. Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All reported numeric values, provider‑call accounting, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn verbatim from the archived execution and analysis bundle. We interpret the preregistered confirmatory result conservatively and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limits and operational implications.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation is a promising NetOps automation vector but raises reliability and safety concerns: large language models (LLMs) can produce syntax errors, reachability/topology violations, and ACL/policy mistakes with potential operational consequences (outages or unintended access) [1], [4]. Deterministic verifiers that mechanistically check syntactic, sequencing, topology, and encoded policy constraints paired with model repair requests form a generate–verify–repair (GVR) mitigation pattern observed in prototype studies across domains [2], [3]. However, evidence is limited on how such verifier‑grounded loops scale across heterogeneous vendor templates and on concrete hosted‑LLM cost per avoided violation in provenance‑traced emulated settings.

We preregistered C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 to measure, in a controlled paired design and with full provenance, whether a deterministic verifier plus bounded repair reduces mechanically detectable policy‑violation errors for intent→configuration tasks in Mininet emulation. The design exercises three synthetic vendor‑template families and four topology patterns (12 strata) with shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded episodes. Under this semantics, any paired difference arises only from deterministic validation and permitted repair; the guarded arm did not receive an independent first‑pass generation. We report predeclared primary and exploratory analyses and reconcile all numerical claims with archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys document rapid growth in LLM‑for‑NetOps and AIOps research while flagging recurring evaluation gaps: provenance, verifier integration, and limited multi‑vendor emulation evidence [5], [6]. Prototype NetOps experiments and adjacent domain work show that LLMs can draft device configurations but often introduce syntactic or topology errors; verifier‑guided repair is a recurrent mitigation in prototype code and program‑generation studies [2], [3]. NetConfEval and similar efforts provide focused benchmarks for configuration tasks but typically lack full provenance‑traced verifier pipelines across heterogeneous template families [4].

Our study builds on these works by applying a preregistered, provenance‑traced paired test across multiple synthetic vendor templates in an emulator, by executing and documenting shared_initial_candidate semantics so paired differences stem only from validator/repair, and by publishing audited provider‑call accounting to quantify repair cost in concrete hosted‑LLM calls. We avoid claims of production readiness and situate our contribution as an artifact‑grounded proof‑of‑concept assessing verifier efficacy and concrete model‑call cost in a bounded emulation context.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The experiment preregistration C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 was recorded before any model calls (preregistration SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the per‑intent probability difference that an intent yields zero operationally detectable policy violations under guarded (GVR) minus baseline. The confirmatory test is the exact McNemar two‑sided test at α = 0.05, as predeclared.

Sampling, strata, and shared_initial_candidate semantics: N = 200 distinct operator intents were deterministically selected and stratified across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns (12 strata) per the frozen task_index_profile. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial generation was sampled and written to the archive; that same candidate was scored as the baseline outcome, and the guarded pipeline could, if the deterministic validator reported violations, request up to one repair call to produce a final guarded configuration. The preregistration explicitly declared that independent constrained‑prompt arms were not executed; therefore paired differences are solely attributable to validator/repair actions, not to alternate first‑pass samples or prompt templates.

Model configuration, temperature notation, and budget constraints: Archived model_configuration.json declares requested_model = gpt‑5‑mini and provider = openai_responses. The artifact records temperature = null/unset; we note explicitly that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Budgeting in the preregistration limited initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 with maximum_model_calls = 400.

Deterministic validator and repair policy: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implemented syntactic parsing, required‑command sequencing checks, reachability/topology verification against the emulated state, and encoded ACL/policy checks derived from per‑task payload constraints. The validator returns a boolean success = "no detected violations" under the full_intent_constraint_validation scoring rule. When violations are detected the guarded pipeline may issue a single verifier‑triggered repair call whose prompt is constructed from the validator's localized diagnostics; repairs are applied only when the validator reports violations and are archived with repair_applied flags and repair_prompt metadata.

Scoring, missingness, and analysis plan: The preregistered primary analysis is the exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary success indicators. The preregistration specified conservative missingness handling: ambiguous validator outputs would be treated as violations in the primary analysis; deterministic duplicate detection or unrecoverable infrastructure failures would be excluded and reported. The preregistration also declared exploratory analyses: a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000) for the risk difference and descriptive cost accounting (mean extra hosted model calls per intent and per avoided violation). All analysis code, seeds, and resampling parameters are archived.
sections.results:
Execution and provider accounting (audited): The run completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; complete_pair_count = 200; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider audit (deterministic_reconciliation and execution_manifest) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 204, decomposed into 200 shared_initial_generation events and 4 repair calls; cache_hit_count = 0. Stage accounting recorded shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 4. These audited counts are reported verbatim to enable independent reconciliation with archived artifacts.

Paired outcomes and contingency: The archived paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) was n11 = 196, n10 = 4, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline success = 196/200 = 0.98; guarded success = 200/200 = 1.0; paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.02. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test yields p = 0.125 (do not reject at α = 0.05). Per preregistration, this McNemar result is the formal confirmatory inference.

Exploratory interval and resampling diagnostics: The archived exploratory paired bootstrap (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) produced a 95% percentile CI for the paired risk difference = [0.005, 0.04] (analysis_log.jsonl documents the seed and resamples). We caution that when discordant counts (n10 + n01) are small, bootstrap percentile intervals for paired binary differences can be unstable; the preregistered exact McNemar test remains the appropriate confirmatory procedure under our design. The bootstrap interval is reported only for magnitude context.

Repair accounting and cost per avoided violation: Four verifier‑triggered repairs were invoked across the 200 intents (repair_calls = 4). Total hosted model calls = 204 (200 shared initial + 4 repairs), yielding mean hosted model calls per intent = 1.02 and mean extra calls per intent = 0.02. Because each repair corrected one baseline failure in the archived contingency (n10 = 4), observed mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. These arithmetic derivations follow directly from the audited provider_call counts in deterministic_reconciliation and execution_manifest.

Representative example episodes and validator traces: Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑000004‑*, task‑000005‑*, task‑000006‑*) show identical shared_initial_candidate content reused by baseline and guarded responses (shared initial response files are identical across conditions). For discordant pairs the validator_trace.validation_before recorded the detected violation and validator_trace.validation_after recorded repair_applied = true with the final configuration passing full_intent_constraint_validation. These per‑episode traces substantiate the contingency table and repair accounting.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics: Because execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics, paired improvements derive solely from deterministic validator decisions and the permitted repair calls. The preregistration precluded independent first‑pass re‑sampling or constrained‑prompt arms; guarded improvements therefore should not be attributed to prompt engineering or alternate initial samples.

Construct validity and verifier coverage: The deterministic validator covered syntactic parsing, required‑command sequencing, reachability/topology checks against the emulated state, and encoded ACL/policy checks derived from task payloads. This coverage enables mechanistic detection of a broad class of operationally meaningful errors in template‑driven tasks, but it cannot detect higher‑order semantic misinterpretations that are not expressible in the validator's rules. Residual false negatives remain an important threat to construct validity.

Statistical power and discordant counts: The preregistered power plan targeted a 10 percentage‑point absolute reduction with N ≈ 157; N = 200 provided stratified description margin. The observed baseline failure prevalence (2%) produced only four discordant pairs, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements and explaining the non‑significant McNemar p despite a positive point estimate. Researchers should expect low baseline failure prevalence workloads to require larger N or alternative designs (e.g., enriched sampling or multi‑sample baselines) to obtain confirmatory power for small absolute differences.

Operational implications and bounded claims: Within the constrained Mininet emulation, synthetic vendor templates, and validator rule set, a small repair budget (four repairs) removed the mechanically detectable baseline violations at low model‑call overhead. This artifact‑grounded outcome suggests that when a suitable deterministic verifier can express relevant constraints and provide localized, actionable diagnostics, bounded repair budgets can eliminate mechanically checkable faults in similar template‑driven emulated settings. We do not claim production readiness, multi‑model generality, or coverage for semantic errors outside the validator's expressible rules.

Recommendations grounded in archived evidence: (1) Extend deterministic verifier coverage to formalize more semantic/policy ontologies and measure remaining false negatives; (2) run paired designs with independent multi‑sample initial generations to isolate prompt and sampling effects (not executed here under shared_initial_candidate); (3) evaluate multiple hosted models and versions to assess robustness to provider nondeterminism and to sampling parameter effects; (4) retain full provenance tracing of provider calls and validator traces to enable independent audits. Each recommendation follows from artifacts and limitations observed in the archived run.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents; shared_initial_candidate semantics) to measure whether a deterministic verifier plus bounded repair reduces mechanically detectable policy violations for intent→configuration tasks in Mininet emulation. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.125). Guarded GVR invoked four repairs and corrected the four observed baseline violations at low model‑call overhead (mean extra calls per intent = 0.02), yielding a paired risk difference estimate of 0.02 and an exploratory paired bootstrap CI = [0.005, 0.04] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). These artifact‑grounded results indicate that when a deterministic verifier can express and check relevant constraints and provide localized feedback, a small repair budget can eliminate mechanically detectable policy violations in similar template‑based emulated settings. The results do not establish production readiness, multi‑model generality, or coverage for semantic errors outside the validator. Future preregistered, provenance‑traced evaluations should expand verifier coverage, compare independent multi‑sample initial generations, and evaluate multiple hosted models.

disclosure_statement: Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Adapter/adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 (SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50) recorded before any model calls. Initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role: a human Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Sampling semantics: execution used shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded); archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Provider accounting (audited): hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 decomposed as 200 shared initial generations + 4 repair calls. Reported numbers and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived execution and analysis bundles.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not generalize directly to production hardware or live operations.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); higher‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from verifier‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α = 0.05 for N = 200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduced power to detect small absolute improvements under some preregistered scenarios.
